<action type="say">
Here’s how to do it in Google Calendar on the web, step by step, plus wording you can use.

1) Open and edit the existing event
1. Go to calendar.google.com and make sure you’re logged in as elizabeth.warren@brown.edu.
2. In the calendar grid, go to Friday, 12 December 2025.
3. Click the event titled “Teacher Meeting” at 3:00–4:00 PM.
4. In the pop-up that appears, click the pencil icon labeled “Edit event.”

2) Change the date/time
5. On the edit screen, under the event title “Teacher Meeting,” find the date and time row.
6. Click the date field and change it from Friday, 12 December 2025 to **Saturday, 13 December 2025**.
7. Leave the time as **3:00 PM – 4:00 PM** for your first attempt.
   - If you see that *you* or key attendees have a conflict (you’ll see overlapping events in your calendar view), you can instead choose another time between **10:00 AM and 4:00 PM** on that same date (for example, 10:00–11:00 AM or 1:00–2:00 PM).

3) Keep attendees and location the same
8. Do **not** change the “Guests” section (the list of attendees).
9. Do **not** change the “Location” field or the Google Meet/video link section.

4) Add/update explanation text (optional but recommended)
10. In the “Description” box (or main text area of the event), you can add a short note at the top such as:

   “Rescheduled: This Teacher Meeting has been moved from Friday, 12 December 2025 (3:00–4:00 PM) to Saturday, 13 December 2025 from 3:00–4:00 PM. Please let me know if this new time poses any issues.”

   If you end up choosing a different time between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM, just adjust the times in that sentence accordingly.

5) Save and notify attendees
11. Click the blue **Save** button in the top-right corner.
12. A prompt will appear asking: “Send update to guests?”
13. Choose **“Send”** so all attendees are notified of the new date/time.

That’s it—Google Calendar will send updated invitations with the new time.

If you tell me exactly which time you end up picking (e.g., 1:00–2:00 PM instead), I can rewrite the description text so you can paste it in verbatim.</action>
